examples.en: I wear an eyeshade when I sleep on a plane.

examples.ko: 게임을 할 때 눈가리개로 눈을 가렸어요.
examples.en: I covered my eyes with a blindfold during the game.
The eyeshade is tied so tight that it's uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 친구가 눈가리개를 한 채 길을 걸었어요.
examples.en: My friend walked down the road wearing a blindfold.

examples.ko: 밝은 방에서는 눈가리개 없이 자기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to sleep without an eyeshade in a bright room.
I put an eyeshade and earplugs in my travel bag.

explain: 잠잘 때 빛을 막는 용도로도 쓰고, 게임이나 놀이에서 눈을 가리는 천에도 써요. 잘 때 쓰는 것은 '수면 안대'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It can be an eyeshade for blocking light while sleeping, or a cloth used to cover the eyes in games. The sleeping kind is also called '수면 안대'.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나니 눈곱이 잔뜩 끼어 있었어요.
examples.en: When I woke up in the morning, my eyes were full of sleep.
I washed my face and wiped off the eye gunk.
My puppy often gets eye discharge.
I rushed out without even wiping the sleep from my eyes.

examples.ko: 눈이 아프고 눈곱이 많이 나와서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My eyes hurt and there was a lot of discharge, so I went to the hospital.
You have some sleep in your eye.

explain: 눈 가장자리에 끼는 것을 말하고, 보통 '눈곱이 끼다', '눈곱을 떼다'로 써요. 아침에 자주 보이지만 눈병이 나면 많이 나오기도 해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람에게 미안한 마음이 눈곱만큼도 없어요.
phrases.en: He doesn't feel the slightest bit sorry.
phrases.nuance_ko: '눈곱'이 아주 작은 것이라서 '조금도 없다'는 강한 부정을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Since eye gunk is tiny, this strongly means 'not even a little'.

explain_en: It is the gunk that collects at the edge of the eye, usually used as '눈곱이 끼다' or '눈곱을 떼다'. You see it often in the morning, but it can increase when you have an eye infection.

examples.en: Grandma took a hard round candy out of her pocket and gave it to me.

examples.ko: 눈깔사탕이 너무 커서 입에 다 안 들어가요.
examples.en: The ball candy is so big it doesn't fit in my mouth.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 문방구에서 눈깔사탕을 자주 사 먹었어요.
examples.en: As a kid I often bought ball candy at the stationery shop.

examples.ko: 동생이 눈깔사탕 하나로 하루 종일 기분이 좋았어요.
examples.en: My little brother was happy all day over one ball candy.
When you put a ball candy in your mouth, your cheek bulges.

examples.ko: 이 가게에는 색깔이 다른 눈깔사탕이 많아요.
examples.en: This shop has lots of ball candies in different colors.

explain: 동그랗고 큰 알사탕을 옛날부터 이렇게 불러요. 요즘은 그냥 '사탕'이나 '알사탕'이라고 많이 하고, 이 말은 옛날 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: This is the old-fashioned name for a big round hard candy. Nowadays people often just say '사탕' or '알사탕', and this word has a nostalgic feel.

examples.en: When I smile, the corners of my eyes turn down.

examples.ko: 화장할 때 눈꼬리에 선을 길게 그렸어요.
examples.en: When doing makeup, I drew a long line at the outer corner of my eye.
His eyes tilt up at the outer corners, so he looks a bit sharp.
As I got older, wrinkles appeared at the corners of my eyes.
My sibling's eyes droop at the corners, so they look gentle.
A makeup style that lifts the outer corners slightly is in fashion.

explain: 귀 쪽에 가까운 눈의 바깥쪽 끝이에요. 반대로 코 쪽 끝은 '눈머리'라고 해요. '눈꼬리가 올라가다/처지다'로 인상을 말할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the outer end of the eye, near the ear. The end near the nose is '눈머리'. It is often used to describe someone's look, as in '눈꼬리가 올라가다/처지다'.

examples.en: The kids roll a lump of snow to make a snowman.
The interest piled up and the debt snowballed.

examples.ko: 언덕 위에서 눈덩이가 아래로 굴러 내려왔어요.
examples.en: A big lump of snow rolled down from the top of the hill.
Even a small lump of snow gets bigger if you keep rolling it.
I packed a snowball with my hands and threw it at my friend.

examples.ko: 걱정이 눈덩이처럼 커져서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My worries snowballed and I couldn't sleep.

explain: 눈을 뭉치거나 굴려서 만든 덩어리예요. 놀이에서는 '눈뭉치'라고도 해요. 비유로 더 많이 쓰여서 '눈덩이처럼 불어나다/커지다'가 자주 나와요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 빚, 피해, 걱정 같은 것이 빠르게 점점 커질 때 써요. 보통 좋지 않은 일에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things like debt, damage or worry grow rapidly. It is usually about bad things.

explain_en: It is a lump of snow that is packed or rolled. For play, people also say '눈뭉치'. It is used a lot figuratively, as in '눈덩이처럼 불어나다/커지다'.

examples.en: I cried all night, so my eyelids are puffy.
I put blue eyeshadow on my eyelids.
After waking up, my eyelids feel heavy.
A mosquito bit me and my eyelid swelled up red.
Please gently press the area above the eye with your hand.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 눈두덩이 두툼해서 인상이 부드러워요.
examples.en: His eyelids are thick, so he gives a soft impression.

explain: 눈 위쪽, 살이 볼록한 곳을 말해요. 보통 '눈두덩이 붓다'처럼 얼굴이 부은 모습을 말할 때 많이 써요. 조사는 '눈두덩이/눈두덩을'로 붙어요.
explain_en: It is the fleshy, rounded part above the eye. It often appears in puffiness expressions like '눈두덩이 붓다'. Particles attach directly: '눈두덩이/눈두덩을'.

en: large round eyes; bright, clear eyes

examples.en: The puppy looked at me with clear, bright eyes.
The child's eyes sparkled like stars.

examples.ko: 사슴 같은 눈망울 때문에 눈길이 갔어요.
examples.en: Her deer-like eyes caught my attention.
Her eyes were filled with tears.

examples.ko: 동생은 큰 눈망울을 굴리며 대답을 기다렸어요.
examples.en: My sibling rolled their big eyes, waiting for an answer.
The cat's round eyes are so cute.

explain: 동그랗고 또렷한 눈을 귀엽게 표현할 때 써요. 주로 아이, 동물, 순한 눈에 쓰고 '맑은/초롱초롱한 눈망울'처럼 자주 말해요. 그냥 '눈'보다 느낌이 부드러워요.
explain_en: It describes round, clear eyes in an endearing way. It is mostly used for children, animals or gentle eyes, as in '맑은/초롱초롱한 눈망울'. It feels softer than plain '눈'.

examples.en: My tear glands are weak, so my eyes often get dry.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 눈물샘을 자극하는 장면이 많아요.
examples.en: That movie has many scenes that tug at your tear glands.
My tear gland got inflamed, so I went to the hospital.
Cutting onions irritates the tear glands.
As people age, tear gland function weakens.

examples.ko: 오늘 드라마는 눈물샘이 터질 만큼 슬펐어요.
examples.en: Today's drama was so sad that I burst into tears.

explain: 눈물이 만들어지는 몸의 기관인데, 일상에서는 '눈물샘을 자극하다', '눈물샘이 터지다'처럼 슬픈 이야기에 많이 써요. '눈물이 나다'보다 조금 과장된 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is the body part that makes tears, but in daily talk it appears in sad-story expressions like '눈물샘을 자극하다' and '눈물샘이 터지다'. It feels a bit more dramatic than '눈물이 나다'.

examples.en: When I woke up, the whole yard was a field of snow.
The puppy plays happily in the snow.
Walking on the snow makes a crunching sound.

examples.ko: 하얀 눈밭 위에 발자국이 길게 남았어요.
examples.en: Long footprints were left on the white snowfield.

examples.ko: 산이 눈밭으로 변해서 등산을 못 했어요.
examples.en: The mountain turned into a snowfield, so we couldn't hike.
The kids lay on the snow and looked at the sky.

explain: 눈이 넓게 쌓인 곳을 말해요. '눈길'은 눈 덮인 길이고, '눈밭'은 길이 아니라 눈이 덮인 넓은 땅이에요. 보통 마당, 들판, 산에 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a wide area covered with snow. '눈길' is a snowy road, while '눈밭' is a wide stretch of snowy ground rather than a path. It is typically used for yards, fields and mountains.

examples.ko: 그 광고는 눈속임이라서 믿으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: That ad is a trick, so you shouldn't believe it.
It's a deception: the packaging is big but there's little inside.
The magician used a sleight of hand to fool the eye.
This isn't a sale; it's a fake discount price.
A trick like that won't last long.
I finished the cleaning half-heartedly, just for show.

explain: 사람의 눈을 속여서 진짜처럼 보이게 하는 일에 써요. 마술에도 쓰지만, 일상에서는 겉만 그럴듯하게 꾸미는 나쁜 행동에 더 많이 써요. '눈속임을 하다/눈속임에 불과하다'로 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for making something look real or better than it is. It can describe magic tricks, but in daily life it more often means a bad, show-only cover-up. Common phrases are '눈속임을 하다' and '눈속임에 불과하다'.

examples.ko: 편지를 읽던 할머니가 눈시울을 붉히며 흐느끼셨어요.
examples.en: Grandma, reading the letter, sobbed with reddened eyes.
Listening to the song, my eyes grew warm with tears.
My friends' eyes got moist at the graduation.
My father's eyes turned slightly red.
My eyes sting with emotion at the touching story.

examples.ko: 눈시울이 젖은 채로 그는 웃어 보였어요.
examples.en: He smiled with his eyes still moist.

explain: 눈 가장자리를 뜻하지만, 거의 감동하거나 슬플 때 눈물이 날 것 같은 모습에만 써요. '눈시울이 붉어지다/뜨거워지다/젖다'가 자주 붙는 말이에요. 단순히 눈 모양을 말할 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 그는 옛 친구를 만나고 눈시울을 붉혔어요.
phrases.en: He teared up when he met his old friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈물이 날 만큼 감동하거나 슬퍼한다는 뜻이고, 눈물이 흐르기 전의 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means being moved or sad enough to get teary, typically before tears actually fall.

explain_en: It means the rim of the eye, but it is used almost only for moments of being moved or sad when tears are about to come. It commonly pairs with '붉어지다/뜨거워지다/젖다'. You don't use it to describe eye shape.

examples.en: I'm going to the snow sledding park with my family this weekend.
The sledding park was full of children.
This sledding park doesn't have an expensive entrance fee.
I lost my gloves at the sledding park.
Every winter the nearby sledding park opens.
It takes about an hour by bus to get to the sledding park.

explain: 스키장과 달리 아이들도 많이 가는 곳으로, 튜브나 작은 썰매를 타고 내려가요. 보통 겨울에만 문을 열어요. 가족 나들이로 자주 가요.
explain_en: Unlike a ski resort, it is a place many children go, where you slide down on a tube or small sled. It is usually open only in winter and is a common family outing.

examples.en: That actor's smiling eyes are really charming.
The baby smiled with its eyes when it saw me.
She greeted me with just a smile of her eyes.

examples.ko: 동생이 눈웃음을 지으면서 용돈을 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: My sibling flashed a sweet smile and asked for pocket money.
With a single smile from his eyes, the mood relaxed.
That person has a pretty eye-smile.

explain: 입보다 눈으로 살짝 웃는 웃음이에요. '눈웃음을 치다'는 호감을 보이거나 애교를 부릴 때 쓰고, 상황에 따라 약간 꾸민 느낌도 줄 수 있어요. 따뜻한 칭찬으로는 '눈웃음이 예쁘다'가 많아요.
explain_en: It is a smile made more with the eyes than the mouth. '눈웃음을 치다' is used when showing affection or acting charming, and can sometimes sound a bit put-on. As a compliment, '눈웃음이 예쁘다' is common.

examples.ko: 아버지가 눈짓하자 동생은 조용히 입을 닫았어요.
examples.en: When Dad signaled with his eyes, my sibling quietly stopped talking.
My friend signaled with his eyes for me to go out.
The teacher signaled with her eyes for us to sit.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 동료에게 눈짓해서 신호를 보냈어요.
examples.en: During the meeting I sent a signal to a coworker with my eyes.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 문 쪽을 보며 눈짓하고 있어요.
examples.en: He is gesturing with his eyes toward the door.
Even though I signaled with my eyes not to say it, it was no use.

explain: 말 대신 눈으로 신호를 보낼 때 써요. 보통 '~라고 눈짓하다'로 내용을 붙이고, 같은 뜻으로 '눈짓을 하다', '눈짓을 보내다'도 많이 써요. 서로 신호를 주고받을 때는 '눈짓을 주고받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when you send a signal with your eyes instead of words. The content is usually added as '~라고 눈짓하다', and '눈짓을 하다' or '눈짓을 보내다' work too. For exchanging signals, say '눈짓을 주고받다'.

en: living under others' scrutiny; eating on sufferance

examples.ko: 친척 집에서 눈칫밥을 먹으며 학교를 다녔어요.
examples.en: I went to school while living at a relative's house, always reading the mood.

examples.ko: 처음 입사했을 때는 눈칫밥을 많이 먹었어요.
examples.en: When I first joined the company, I had to watch others' moods a lot.
I didn't want to be walking on eggshells, so I became independent early.
I only ate meals under their watchful eyes in that house before I left.

examples.ko: 눈칫밥 먹는 신세가 되니까 마음이 불편해요.
examples.en: Being in a position of living on others' sufferance makes me uneasy.

examples.ko: 아이가 눈칫밥을 먹지 않게 잘 챙겨 주세요.
examples.en: Please take care of the child so he doesn't feel unwelcome.

explain: 남의 눈치를 보며 불편하게 먹거나 지내야 하는 상황을 말해요. 보통 '눈칫밥을 먹다'로 쓰고 실제 밥이 아니어도 괜찮아요. 기댈 곳이 없어 눈치를 보는 안쓰러운 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 저는 어릴 때 삼촌 집에서 눈칫밥을 먹고 자랐어요.
phrases.en: I grew up at my uncle's house feeling like a burden.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 집이나 직장에서 마음 편히 지내지 못하고 눈치를 보며 산다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means being unable to relax at someone else's home or workplace and living while watching their reactions.
phrases.en_equiv: to walk on eggshells; to live on sufferance

explain_en: It refers to a situation where you must eat or live uncomfortably, watching others' moods. It is usually '눈칫밥을 먹다', and it need not involve actual food. It carries a pitiful sense of having no place to lean on.

en: be scorched; burn; burn to the bottom of a pot or pan

examples.en: The rice stuck and burned onto the bottom of the pot.

examples.ko: 불을 세게 켜면 고기가 팬에 눌어붙어요.
examples.en: If you turn up the heat, the meat sticks and burns on the pan.

examples.ko: 눌어붙은 찌꺼기를 닦는 데 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a long time to scrub off the burnt-on residue.

examples.ko: 기름을 안 두르면 계란이 눌어붙을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't add oil, the egg can stick and burn.

examples.ko: 국이 눌어붙지 않게 가끔 저어 주세요.
examples.en: Please stir the soup now and then so it doesn't stick and burn.

examples.ko: 냄비에 우유가 눌어붙어서 탄 냄새가 나요.
examples.en: Milk has burned onto the pot, so it smells burnt.

explain: 열 때문에 음식이 그릇에 붙으면서 조금 타는 것을 말해요. '타다'는 많이 까맣게 태우는 느낌이고, '눌어붙다'는 바닥에 딱 붙은 상태에 초점이 있어요. '눌어붙은 밥', '눌은밥'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes food sticking to a pot or pan and slightly burning from heat. '타다' suggests blackened burning, while '눌어붙다' focuses on being stuck to the bottom. You also see '눌어붙은 밥' and '눌은밥'.

examples.ko: 밥을 하고 남은 눌은밥에 물을 부어 끓였어요.
examples.en: I poured water on the scorched rice left over from cooking and boiled it.
Grandma made scorched rice into a warm rice-water drink.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 먹던 눌은밥이 가끔 생각나요.
examples.en: I sometimes think of the scorched rice I ate as a kid.
The scorched rice at the bottom of the pot tastes nutty.

examples.ko: 눌은밥은 불리면 부드럽게 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can eat scorched rice softly once you soak it.
Scorched rice came out as a dessert at the restaurant.

explain: 솥 바닥에 눌어붙어 누렇게 된 밥이에요. 여기에 물을 붓고 끓여 먹으면 구수해요. 비슷한 말로 '누룽지'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is rice that has stuck to the bottom of the pot and turned golden brown. Boiling it with water gives a nutty taste. A similar word is '누룽지'.

en: comfortably; in a relaxed manner; at ease

examples.en: On weekend mornings I drink coffee at a leisurely pace.
We have plenty of time, so please wait calmly.

examples.ko: 그는 소파에 느긋이 앉아서 책을 읽었어요.
examples.en: He sat comfortably on the sofa and read a book.
I took a relaxed walk and looked around the neighborhood.
You don't need to rush; you can get ready at ease.

examples.ko: 휴가 때는 느긋이 늦잠을 자고 싶어요.
examples.en: On vacation I want to sleep in leisurely.

explain: 서두르지 않고 마음이 편한 모습을 말해요. '천천히'는 속도 중심이고, '느긋이'는 마음의 여유가 느껴지는 말이에요. 같은 뜻으로 '느긋하게'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It describes being unhurried with a calm mind. '천천히' focuses on speed, while '느긋이' suggests a relaxed state of mind. '느긋하게' is also commonly used with the same meaning.

examples.ko: 저는 걸음이 느려서 친구들이 느림보라고 불러요.
examples.en: I walk slowly, so my friends call me a slowpoke.
The tortoise is famous for being slow.

examples.ko: 저 느림보 좀 보세요, 아직도 신발을 신고 있어요.
examples.en: Look at that slowpoke, still putting on his shoes.

examples.ko: 동생은 밥 먹을 때 느림보가 돼요.
examples.en: My sibling turns into a slowpoke when eating.
I took a super slow bus and was late for the appointment.
My son is like a slowpoke every morning.

explain: 행동이 느린 사람이나 동물을 가볍게 놀릴 때 써요. 친한 사이에는 장난스럽게 쓰지만, 모르는 사람에게 하면 실례일 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '굼벵이', 반대로 '날쌘돌이'가 있어요.
explain_en: It lightly teases a slow person or animal. Among close people it sounds playful, but saying it to a stranger can be rude. A similar word is '굼벵이', and an opposite is '날쌘돌이'.

examples.en: Grandpa's walk is slow and unhurried.
On hot days both body and mind become sluggish.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말투가 느릿느릿해서 답답할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: His way of speaking is slow, so it can be frustrating at times.

examples.ko: 동작이 느릿느릿한 고양이가 창가에 누워 있어요.
examples.en: A cat with lazy movements is lying by the window.
The computer is sluggish today.
My slow-moving sibling suddenly started running.

explain: 행동이나 말이 아주 느리고 굼뜬 모습이에요. 실제로는 부사 '느릿느릿'을 훨씬 많이 써서 '느릿느릿 걷다'처럼 말해요. 형용사는 상태를 설명할 때 써요.
explain_en: It describes behavior or speech that is very slow and dragging. In reality the adverb '느릿느릿' is used far more often, as in '느릿느릿 걷다'. The adjective form is for describing a state.

examples.en: Grandma's way of speaking is always warm and slow.
Slow music was playing, so I felt sleepy.

examples.ko: 그 가게 주인은 행동이 조금 느릿해요.
examples.en: The shop owner moves a little slowly.
The river is flowing slowly.

examples.ko: 더워서 그런지 오늘은 모든 게 느릿해 보여요.
examples.en: Maybe because of the heat, everything looks slow today.

examples.ko: 느릿한 걸음으로 공원을 한 바퀴 돌았어요.
examples.en: I walked around the park once at a leisurely pace.

explain: '느리다'보다 여유 있고 느긋한 느낌이 있어서 걸음, 말씨, 음악의 속도를 부드럽게 표현할 때 써요. '느릿느릿하다'보다 덜 답답한 느낌이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '느리다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It feels more leisurely than '느리다', so it softly describes the pace of steps, speech or music. It sounds less frustrating than '느릿느릿하다'. In everyday talk, '느리다' is used more.

examples.en: I put oyster mushrooms in the soybean paste stew.
Oyster mushrooms are tasty if you tear them and stir-fry them.
I bought a bag of oyster mushrooms at the mart.
The oyster mushrooms are fresh, so the aroma is good.
Add oyster mushrooms and tofu to the hot pot.
I often eat stir-fried oyster mushrooms as a side dish.

explain: 한국 요리에서 자주 쓰는 버섯이고 찌개, 전골, 볶음에 많이 들어가요. 표고버섯보다 부드럽고 향이 약해요. 그냥 '느타리'라고도 해요.
explain_en: This mushroom is common in Korean cooking and goes into stews, hot pots and stir-fries. It is softer and milder in aroma than shiitake ('표고버섯'). People also say just '느타리'.

examples.ko: 저는 마흔에 대학에 들어간 늦깎이 학생이에요.
examples.en: I'm a late-starting student who entered college at forty.
That writer made a late debut.
Becoming a parent late in life, I'm more careful.
My father learned to drive late in life.
I started late, but I worked hard and caught up.
There are quite a few late-starting students in the class too.

explain: 보통보다 늦게 어떤 일을 시작하거나 성공한 사람에게 써요. 놀리는 말이 아니라 그래도 열심히 한다는 긍정적인 느낌이 있어요. '늦깎이 학생', '늦깎이 데뷔'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It refers to someone who starts or succeeds at something later than usual. It is not a tease and often carries a positive sense of working hard anyway. Common uses are '늦깎이 학생' and '늦깎이 데뷔'.

en: late summer heat; lingering summer heat

examples.en: Even though it's September, the lingering summer heat continues.

examples.ko: 올해는 늦더위 때문에 가을옷을 못 입었어요.
examples.en: This year I couldn't wear autumn clothes because of the late heat.
The late heat is severe, so I still turn on the air conditioner.
They say the lingering heat will ease from tomorrow.
I'm worn out by the late heat and have no appetite.
Even after Chuseok, the late heat hasn't gone away.

explain: 여름이 지났는데도 남아 있는 더위를 말해요. 뉴스나 날씨 이야기에서 '늦더위가 기승을 부리다', '늦더위가 이어지다'로 자주 나와요. 반대로 봄에 늦게까지 남은 추위는 '늦추위'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means heat that remains after summer should be over. In news and weather talk you see '늦더위가 기승을 부리다' and '늦더위가 이어지다'. The cold that lingers into spring is '늦추위'.

en: child born late in the parents' life

examples.en: I'm a late-born child whom my parents had at forty.
My much-younger sibling gets all the family's love.
Grandma cherished her youngest son, born late in life, the most.

examples.ko: 늦둥이를 키우는 부모님은 늘 체력이 걱정이에요.
examples.en: Parents raising a late-born child always worry about their stamina.
The late-born child in our house is still in elementary school.

examples.ko: 그 집은 첫째와 늦둥이가 스무 살 차이래요.
examples.en: They say the eldest and the late-born child there are twenty years apart.

explain: '막내'와 달라요. 막내는 순서상 마지막 아이이고, 늦둥이는 부모가 나이 들어 낳아서 형제와 나이 차가 큰 아이예요. 보통 귀염받는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It differs from '막내'. 막내 is simply the last child in order, while 늦둥이 is a child born when the parents are older, often with a big age gap from siblings. It usually carries a sense of being doted on.

examples.en: I turn into a sleepyhead every weekend.
My older brother is a well-known late riser.
It's hard waking up my sleepyhead son.

examples.ko: 주말이면 늦잠꾸러기 친구가 열 시까지 자요.
examples.en: On weekends my sleepyhead friend sleeps until ten.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 늦잠꾸러기라서 학교에 자주 늦었어요.
examples.en: As a kid I was a late sleeper, so I was often late for school.

examples.ko: 늦잠꾸러기도 아침 운동을 하면 달라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even a sleepyhead can change by exercising in the morning.

explain: 늦잠을 자는 사람을 귀엽게 놀릴 때 써요. 가족이나 친구 사이에서 장난스럽게 쓰고, 어른에게는 쓰지 않아요. '-꾸러기'는 어떤 특징이 강한 사람에게 붙는 말이에요.
explain_en: It teases someone who oversleeps in a cute way. It is used playfully among family and friends, but not to elders. The ending '-꾸러기' attaches to a person with a strong trait.

examples.en: Triangles and squares are both polygons.
We learned the names of polygons in math class.

examples.ko: 이 도형은 변이 여섯 개인 다각형이에요.
examples.en: This shape is a polygon with six sides.
Try finding the sum of the angles of the polygon.
Please draw a big polygon on paper and bring it.
A circle has no sides, so it isn't a polygon.

explain: 변이 세 개 이상인 도형을 모두 부르는 말이에요. 수학 시간에 주로 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '삼각형, 사각형'처럼 각각 말해요. '다각형'은 여러 각이 있는 모양이에요.
explain_en: It is the general term for any shape with three or more sides. It mostly appears in math class, while in daily talk people name shapes like '삼각형' and '사각형'. It means a figure with many angles.

examples.en: This app supports multiple languages, so it's convenient.
A multilingual notice is posted at the entrance.
Our company website was made in multiple languages.

examples.ko: 다국어 메뉴판 덕분에 외국인 손님도 편하게 주문해요.
examples.en: Thanks to the multilingual menu, foreign guests order easily.

examples.ko: 그 사전은 다국어 번역 기능이 있어요.
examples.en: That dictionary has a multilingual translation feature.
Multilingual announcements play at the airport.

explain: 여러 나라 말을 한꺼번에 쓰거나 지원할 때 써요. '다국어 지원', '다국어 안내'처럼 뒤에 다른 말과 붙어서 많이 나와요. 사람이 여러 언어를 할 때는 '여러 언어를 하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when many languages are used or supported at once. It often attaches to other words, as in '다국어 지원' and '다국어 안내'. For a person who speaks several languages, people say '여러 언어를 하다'.

examples.en: He made a phone call in a rush.
The child called his mother urgently.
I fell while running in a hurry.
My friend asked me urgently for help.
The firefighters rushed urgently to the scene.
I opened the door hurriedly, but nobody was there.

explain: 일이 급해서 마음의 여유가 없는 모습을 말해요. '급히'는 속도나 시간이 급할 때도 쓰지만, '다급히'는 마음이 몹시 급하고 조급한 느낌이 더 강해요. 주로 부르다, 뛰다, 말하다 같은 동작과 함께 써요.
explain_en: It describes acting with no room to breathe because things are pressing. '급히' can mean just quick, but '다급히' feels more anxious and desperate. It is typically used with actions like calling, running or speaking.

examples.en: I have an exam the week after next.
I plan to move the month after next.
Please get off at the station after the next one.
The stop after the next is my house.
I have to give a presentation in the class after next.
When should we set the appointment after the next one?

explain: '다음'의 다음을 뜻하며 주, 달, 역, 차례처럼 순서가 있는 말 앞에 써요. 날짜는 '모레'나 '글피'처럼 따로 있는 말도 있어요. '다다음 주'는 '다음 주'보다 한 주 뒤예요.
explain_en: It means the one after '다음' (next), and is placed before ordered nouns like weeks, months, stations and turns. For days there are separate words like '모레' and '글피'. '다다음 주' is one week after '다음 주'.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 다단계 판매로 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: That company got in trouble over multilevel sales.

examples.ko: 친구가 다단계 사업을 같이 하자고 해서 거절했어요.
examples.en: A friend asked me to join a multilevel business and I refused.
You must be careful about the multilevel method from the start.

examples.ko: 이 로켓은 다단계 구조로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This rocket has a multistage structure.

examples.ko: 다단계 업체에 돈을 맡겼다가 손해를 봤어요.
examples.en: He entrusted money to a multilevel firm and lost out.
They are selling the new product through multilevel distribution.

explain: 여러 단계로 이루어진 구조를 말하지만, 일상에서는 사람을 모아 물건을 파는 '다단계 판매'의 뜻으로 가장 많이 써요. 이때는 조심하라는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 로켓이나 과정처럼 단계가 여럿이라는 뜻으로도 쓰여요.
explain_en: It means a structure of several stages, but in daily life it is most commonly '다단계 판매' (multilevel sales), which carries a cautionary, negative tone. It can also mean multistage things like rockets or processes.

examples.en: I put money into a savings account each month.
I pay the rent on the 25th of every month.
The money that goes out each month is too much.
I send pocket money to my grandmother every month.

examples.ko: 다달이 한 권씩 책을 읽기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to read one book each month.
The magazine is delivered to my house monthly.

explain: '매달'과 같은 뜻이지만 조금 더 옛날 느낌이 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '매달'을 더 많이 쓰고, '다달이'는 글이나 정겨운 말투에 나와요. 매주는 '주마다', 매일은 '날마다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '매달' but sounds a little more old-fashioned. In everyday talk '매달' is more common, while '다달이' appears in writing or a homey tone. Similar patterns include '주마다' (weekly) and '날마다' (daily).

examples.en: I got a sty on my eye, so I went to the hospital.
My eye is swollen because of a sty.
I often get styes when I'm tired.

examples.ko: 다래끼가 난 눈은 손으로 만지지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't touch an eye with a sty using your hands.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 다래끼에 약을 처방해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor prescribed medicine for the sty.
A sty usually goes down after a few days.

explain: 눈꺼풀 가장자리에 빨갛게 부어오르는 염증이에요. '다래끼가 나다'라고 말하고, '생기다'도 써요. 눈을 비비지 말라는 말을 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It is a red, swollen inflammation on the edge of the eyelid. You say '다래끼가 나다', and '생기다' also works. People often hear advice not to rub their eyes.

examples.en: I do the ironing on Sunday evening.
I'm clumsy at ironing, so the shirt got wrinkled.

examples.ko: 다리미질 후에는 꼭 전원을 꺼야 해요.
examples.en: After ironing you must turn off the power.
My mother is very skilled at ironing.
I listened to a drama while ironing.
Ironing takes longer than you'd think.

explain: 다리미로 옷을 펴는 일이에요. 보통 '다리미질을 하다'라고 말하고, '다림질'이라고도 해요. 말할 때는 '옷을 다리다'라고 하는 경우도 많아요.
explain_en: It is the work of smoothing clothes with an iron. You usually say '다리미질을 하다', and '다림질' is also used. In speech, people also often say '옷을 다리다'.

examples.en: I iron my shirt every morning.
My mother is ironing the school uniform.
I pressed my suit before the interview.
I burned my hand while ironing.
It has many wrinkles, so I need to iron it.
If you iron slowly, the clothes become neat.

explain: 일상에서는 같은 뜻으로 '다리다'를 많이 써요. '옷을 다리다'가 더 자연스럽고, '다리미질하다'는 일을 하는 동작이라는 느낌이 있어요. '다림질하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: In daily speech, '다리다' is often used for the same meaning. '옷을 다리다' sounds more natural, while '다리미질하다' feels like naming the chore itself. '다림질하다' is also used.

examples.ko: 이 방은 다목적으로 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can use this room for multiple purposes.
A new multipurpose hall was built at the school.

examples.ko: 다목적 칼이라서 요리할 때도 쓰고 캠핑할 때도 써요.
examples.en: It's a multipurpose knife, so I use it for cooking and camping.

examples.ko: 이 다목적 청소기는 차 안도 닦을 수 있어요.
examples.en: This multipurpose vacuum can clean the inside of a car too.
There is a multipurpose sports ground in the neighborhood.

examples.ko: 다목적 공간이라서 행사도 하고 회의도 해요.
examples.en: It's a multipurpose space, so we hold events and meetings there.

explain: 한 가지가 아니라 여러 가지 일에 쓸 수 있다는 말로, 주로 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며요. '다목적 강당', '다목적 공간'처럼 쓰고, 물건에는 '다용도'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means usable for several jobs, not just one, and mostly modifies a following noun, as in '다목적 강당' and '다목적 공간'. For items, '다용도' is used more often.

examples.en: I live on the second floor of a multi-unit house.

examples.ko: 다세대 주택은 아파트보다 월세가 싼 편이에요.
examples.en: Rent in a multi-unit house tends to be cheaper than in an apartment.
There are many multi-unit buildings in this alley.

examples.ko: 다세대 주택으로 이사 가려고 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking into moving to a multi-unit house.
Our home is a three-story multi-unit building.
Many multi-unit houses have narrow parking lots.

explain: 한 건물에 여러 가구가 따로 사는 작은 규모의 집을 말하며, 보통 '다세대 주택'으로 써요. 아파트보다 작고 '빌라'라고도 불러요. 부동산에서는 '다가구'와 구분해서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a small building where several households live separately, usually '다세대 주택'. It is smaller than an apartment and is also called '빌라'. In real estate it is sometimes distinguished from '다가구'.

examples.en: The company diversified its products and customers increased.
The restaurant decided to diversify its menu.
It's safer to diversify your sources of income.
The school is diversifying its teaching methods.
To diversify the customer base, we need promotion.
After I diversified my investments, the risk went down.

explain: 방식, 상품, 종류 같은 것을 여러 가지로 늘릴 때 써요. 뉴스나 회사 이야기에서 많이 나오는 딱딱한 말이라 일상에서는 '다양하게 하다'라고 풀어 말하기도 해요. '다양해지다'는 저절로 여러 가지가 되는 것이에요.
explain_en: It is used when you expand something such as methods, products or types into more varieties. It's a formal word common in news and business, so in daily talk people may say '다양하게 하다'. '다양해지다' means becoming varied on its own.

examples.en: These scissors are multipurpose, so they're really convenient.
I bought a multipurpose table and use it as a desk too.

examples.ko: 다용도 칼 하나면 캠핑 준비가 끝나요.
examples.en: One multipurpose knife is enough for camping.

examples.ko: 다용도로 쓸 수 있는 가방을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a bag that can be used in many ways.

examples.ko: 이 세제는 다용도라서 주방과 욕실에 다 써요.
examples.en: This detergent is multipurpose, so I use it in the kitchen and bathroom.
A multipurpose chest of drawers makes it easy to organize.

explain: 한 물건을 여러 용도로 쓸 수 있을 때 써요. '다목적'과 비슷하지만 물건이나 도구에는 '다용도'를 더 자주 쓰고, 공간이나 시설에는 '다목적'을 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used when one item serves several uses. It is close to '다목적', but '다용도' is more often used for items and tools, while '다목적' is common for spaces and facilities.

examples.en: The washing machine is in the utility room.
I put the cleaning tools together in the utility room.
The utility room in our house is a bit narrow.

examples.ko: 다용도실 문을 열면 세제 냄새가 나요.
examples.en: When you open the utility room door, there's a smell of detergent.
I hung the laundry in the utility room.
This apartment is nice because the utility room is spacious.

explain: 주방 옆이나 베란다에 있는 작은 방으로, 세탁기, 청소 도구, 짐을 두는 곳이에요. 영어의 'utility room'과 비슷해요. 아파트를 구할 때 집 구조에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a small room next to the kitchen or on the veranda for the washing machine, cleaning tools and storage. It is similar to a 'utility room'. It often comes up when describing a home's layout while apartment hunting.
